findings.text: remove_worker_scratch prints to stdout at :7708, :7712 and :7719 and is reachable from the promotion path, which no test on this node's gate drives; it is outside this node's stated measure of more than one document or non-JSON text but would corrupt a caller that parsed its output.
the peer-channel entry prints its own JSON document to stdout at :2933; it is a second stdout entry point, not on crew_dispatch's call path, and this node may not edit it.

the launch path's config-error outcome emits no JSON document at all (empty stdout), a zero-document shape outside this node's stated measure; a caller that parses stdout reads a failure of a different kind than the section describes.

item_verdicts.call_sites: reckon/cli.py:1721 applies _holds_stdout_for_one_document to crew_dispatch; reckon/cli.py:987 is _emit, whose getattr(sys.stdout, 'payload_stream', sys.stdout) reaches the held-aside stream.
item_verdicts.diff: read 74bb83d4 and 7c41483e against base 9b66ff8a; cli.py adds _OneDocumentStdout, _single_document_stdout and _holds_stdout_for_one_document with a payload_stream read in _emit, the test file adds the reproduction, docs adds the landed fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: section 29's done_when is met by tests/test_dispatch_stdout_is_one_document.py, which drives eight outcome paths through click's CliRunner with stdout and stderr captured separately and asserts json.loads(stdout) parses.
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal — one decodable document on stdout whatever code beneath the command prints — is met by the stdout-notice channel applied to crew_dispatch, with the payload reaching the caller through the held-aside stream.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records base 3 failed/229 passed/1 skipped and head 1 failed/231 passed/1 skipped with named logs, a base survey of the stdout writers beneath the command, and an executed negative control with its red log.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the manifest's declared paths; both commits touch only reckon/cli.py, tests/test_dispatch_stdout_is_one_document.py and the docs fragment, all inside them.

justifications.durability: the guard is structural — it wraps the whole click command rather than a block of its body — and tests/test_dispatch_stdout_is_one_document.py asserts both halves (stdout parses, the injected notice lands on stderr and not stdout); logs/negative-control.log reddens the presence case at base with json.decoder.JSONDecodeError, and an independent probe confirms print, click.echo and sys.stdout.write all reach the notice channel.
justifications.evidence: base-arm.log (revision 9b66ff8a) records 3 failed/229 passed/1 skipped at EXIT=1 and head-arm-2.log (revision 74bb83d4) records 1 failed/231 passed/1 skipped at EXIT=1, the head failure being an id the base already fails, so added_failure_count is 0; an independent base extraction with the test file added reproduces the presence-case JSONDecodeError, and the head extraction passes it.
justifications.fit: the wrapper follows the module's existing single-emission idiom around _emit rather than adding a second JSON path, and _emit's getattr(sys.stdout, 'payload_stream', sys.stdout) is a small implicit protocol on the stream object.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the node goal is a caller's json.loads(stdout) seeing exactly one document; crew_dispatch is wrapped by _holds_stdout_for_one_document (reckon/cli.py:1721) so every write beneath the command forwards to stderr while _emit (reckon/cli.py:987) writes the single payload to the real stdout, and an independent run of the new test file at the reviewed head passes 8/8.
justifications.scope_discipline: the two commits touch only reckon/cli.py, tests/test_dispatch_stdout_is_one_document.py and the docs evidence fragment, all inside the manifest's declared write paths, and the only failure the head arm carries was failing at base too.
